To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Alginate produced by Azo. vinelandii was degraded by the action of the Alginate lyase activity encoded by the alginate biosynthesis gene algL.
the alginate lyases encoded by the alginate biosynthesis gene clusters of Azotobacter species are responsible for the degradation of alginate produced during the exponential phase of the culture.
the alginate lyases AlgL and AlgE are responsible for the drop in the mean molecular weight of alginates produced by A. vinelandii.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the role of alginate lyase in A. vinelandiialginate metabolism, which is relevant for biotechnological applications of this microorganism.
the production of a higher quality alginate by an A. vinemandii algL mutant, strain SML2.
a new approach to the improvement of alginate production by A. vinemandii.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AlgL activity is not necessary to produce high-molecular-weight alginate by A. vineladni, but that it does contribute to the degradation of alginate during culture.
the alginate lyases are not involved in the alginate biosynthesis, but they are responsible of alginate depolymerization.
the alginate produced by the mutant SML2 was of higher quality, in terms of molecular weight and alginate lyase degradation, than that of the wild-type strain ATCC 9064.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the deletion of the alginate lyases gene from the A. vinelandiialginate biosynthesis pathway is a useful approach to increase the mean molecular weight of the alginate produced by the strain.
the alginate produced by SML2 is a better quality product than the one produced by the parental strain.
we have shown that the alginate lyases of A. vineladni are involved in the degradation of alginate and that the alginate produced by the mutant is more suitable for industrial application.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the alginate produced by the algL mutant strain has a higher mean molecular weight, and that it is more viscous than alginate produced by wild-type A. vinelandiii.

the alginate lyases are not essential enzymes in the alginate biosynthesis pathway, and their absence leads to an increase in the molecular weight and viscosity of the alginate produced by Azobacter vinelandiii.
alginate produced by an A. vinelndii mutant unable to express alginate lyase is of higher quality, in terms of molecular weight, than alginate produced by the parental strain.
